title: Elodie and the Detention
premise: Mirabel Reyes has spent two decades hiding behind an anonymous coding account that keeps surfacing truths about the elite Ashgrove Academy's school board—truths someone else seems to know he knows. When his best friend and fellow whistleblower Priya vanishes, leaving only a ring of keys to the school's sealed 1980s records annex, Mirabel must finally step out of the shadows. Following Priya's trail through buried abuse scandals, forged inheritances, and a board that has protected its own for forty years, he discovers Priya didn't run—she was silenced, and she left him the keys on purpose. In the end, Mirabel sacrifices his anonymity at a public board hearing, streaming the annex archives live, and finds Priya alive in hiding, choosing a found family of fellow survivors over the safety he can never return to.
about_author: Beatrix Eriksen is a former boarding-school teacher who spent six years documenting institutional cover-ups before turning to fiction. She writes young adult thrillers about quiet kids who refuse to stay quiet, from a farmhouse in coastal Maine.

chapters.title: The Account That Knew
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. We meet him at 3 a.m., maintaining @ashgrove_truth, an anonymous account that has just posted its most dangerous thread yet about the school board's sealed files. His careful, controlled life is sketched: day job, encrypted everything, no close ties except Priya. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as discipline—the cost of twenty years of invisibility.

chapters.title: Keys on the Kitchen Table
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Priya misses their weekly dinner—a first in fifteen years. At her apartment he finds it ransacked-but-tidy: nothing stolen except her laptop, and on the table, a labeled ring of keys to the academy's decommissioned records annex. A note reads only '1987.' Emotional beat: dread crystallizing into resolve; the moment hiding stops being possible.

chapters.title: What the Annex Remembers
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, intercut with flashbacks to his and Priya's student years. Using the keys, he enters the annex and finds boxes the board officially 'destroyed' in 1994—complaints, medical reports, hush payments tied to a beloved deceased headmaster. Emotional beat: vertigo of inheritance; the past is not past, and it was left for him deliberately.

chapters.title: The Board Knows Your Name
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. A lawyer representing the board appears at his workplace, politely offering a settlement for 'harassment via anonymous accounts'—proving they've unmasked him partially and are watching. He realizes posting the thread triggered them, and that Priya vanished after contacting the same lawyer. Emotional beat: paranoia sharpening into strategy; fear becomes fuel.

chapters.title: Everyone Priya Ever Saved
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Mirabel and Dana Okafor, a former Ashgrove student Priya had quietly helped years ago. Mirabel follows Priya's pattern of small kindnesses and finds a loose network of alumni—each holding one fragment of evidence, none knowing the others. Emotional beat: tentative warmth; the first hint that found family is both the method and the reward.

chapters.title: The Inheritance Clause
chapters.summary: Dana's POV. The network decodes the '1987' clue: the headmaster willed his estate—and control of a trust funding the school—to the first person who could prove the cover-up, a clause the board buried by declaring the documents destroyed. The inheritance isn't money; it's standing, the legal right to compel disclosure. Emotional beat: hope with teeth; the stakes become winnable.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. His apartment is broken into; his employer fires him; a threatening voicemail references Priya in the present tense—he's alive. The board offers one last deal: silence in exchange for Priya's location. Mirabel almost takes it, then hears Priya's voice in his memory: 'Careful was always just scared with better branding.' Emotional beat: the dark night; grief, temptation, refusal.

chapters.title: Quorum
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converge. The alumni network executes Mirabel's plan: while the board holds its annual public meeting, Dana requests recognition under the trust clause, forcing the board to either produce the 'destroyed' records or admit fraud on the record. Meanwhile Mirabel infiltrates the annex to digitize everything before the board's cleaners arrive. Emotional beat: rising crescendo; ordinary people moving in perfect, terrified coordination.

chapters.title: Elodie
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Cornered in the annex by the board's fixer, Mirabel goes live-streaming instead of running, reading case numbers aloud as officers—tipped by Dana—arrive. He reveals his name and face to end anonymity forever. The fixer cracks and reveals Priya's location: she faked her disappearance when the board moved to kill her, waiting for proof the network could finish what she started. Emotional beat: climax; identity claimed at last, loudly, irreversibly.

chapters.title: So Careful It Hurts
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, weeks later. The trust is activated, the board resigns en masse, and the annex becomes a survivor-led archive. Priya returns, changed and unapologetic, and the network gathers for the first time in one room—not as co-conspirators but as family. Mirabel deletes @ashgrove_truth, no longer needing a mask. Emotional beat: resolution; inheritance redefined as belonging, and visibility chosen over safety.
